content.title: Neighborhood Leader Network
content.summary: The Neighborhood Leader Network (NLN) in Arvada aims to develop and support neighborhood leaders who volunteer to represent their communities and collaborate with the city. To become a Neighborhood Leader, individuals must enroll their neighborhood in the Neighbors Connected Program, allowing them to participate in quarterly meetings that cover various community topics and initiatives. Recent meetings have included service projects, discussions on supporting older adults, and emergency preparedness training, with the next meeting scheduled for September 2026.
content.body:
![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=4384)

The Neighborhood Leader Network (NLN) exists to develop and support neighborhood leaders and their neighborhoods. A Neighborhood can have multiple registered Neighborhood Leaders.

**To become a Neighborhood Leader, your neighborhood must be enrolled in the Neighbors Connected Program. Not sure what enrolling in a neighborhood group entails? [Learn more on the Neighbors Connected page](/482/Neighbors-Connected).**

## Become a Neighborhood Leader

Neighborhood Leaders are volunteers who represent their neighbors and work in collaboration with the City of Arvada. Leaders have an opportunity to participate in quarterly meetings where community partners and subject matter experts share information about topics that affect the quality of life in your neighborhoods. By participating in the NLN, you will learn to become a more effective leader in your neighborhood and beyond. The following are examples of topics this group has discussed recently:

- Neighborhood Conflict Resolution
- Neighborhood Preparedness
- How to organize successful block parties
- Understanding neighbor and neighborhood demographics

## Upcoming Neighborhood Leader Network meetings

**The next Neighborhood Leader Network meeting will take place in September 2026.**Details will be posted on this page once the meeting has been finalized. 

## Recap of Prior Meetings

### June 3, 2026 - Apex Community Recreation Center

Neighborhood Leaders completed a service project, building 65 move-in kits for neighbors exiting homelessness in Arvada. Leaders also participated in an interactive exercise with the City's Homelessness Program Team which simulated the barriers to obtaining a Colorado ID card, an important step to securing employment and housing.

### March 11, 2026 - Pomona High School

Neighborhood Leaders participated in discussion groups about how to support the older adults in their neighborhoods and in their lives. Discussion groups were led by experts from A Little Help, Arvada Emergency Management, Arvada Fire, Arvada Police, AARP, APEX Park and Recreation District, 1st Judicial District Attorney's Office, Jeffco Public Health, and Seniors Resource Center.

### October 8, 2025 - Colorado Gives Foundation

Neighborhood Leaders shared ideas for how the Colorado Gives Foundation can support community building in Arvada and throughout Jefferson County. Colorado Gives Leadership will be taking these ideas forward into their planning for 2026 to continue supporting a thriving Arvada!

### August 27, 2025 - Arvada Fire Training Center

Neighborhood Leaders received interactive presentations from Arvada Fire, Arvada Police and Maple Valley HOA Neighborhood Leader Gina Hallisey. Attendees also received Emergency Preparedness folders filled with resources, information and tools to prepare for emergencies.

### June 10, 2025 - Storyline Church

Neighborhood Leaders participated in discussion groups led by their peers to exchange ideas about how to organize successful neighborhood gatherings. These gatherings include block parties, movie nights, concerts and neighborhood projects.

### March 5, 2025 - Arvada High School

Neighborhood Leaders collaborated with experts from Jefferson County Public Health and received a presentation featuring their County [Health Improvement Plan](https://www.jeffco.us/3736/County-Health-Improvement-Plan) (CHIP). Neighborhood Leaders provided community feedback on CHIP priorities to improve physical and mental health outcomes for Arvadans.

### November 12, 2024 - Arvada Library

Neighborhood Leaders participated in a game of Local Government Trivia led by Director of Communications and Engagement, Rachael Kuroiwa. Leaders learned about how land is zoned, how property taxes are collected and many more topics that affect the community. The role of government leaders, city staff and residents were also discussed and nuances were highlighted about how processes and systems in local government function.

### August 27, 2024 - APEX Center

Neighborhood Leaders engaged in a presentation from the Arvada Fire Protection District and [CERT](https://www.arvadaco.gov/684/Arvada-CERT) (Community Emergency Response Team) about emergency preparedness for neighborhoods. Emergencies come in all shapes and sizes and Neighborhood Leaders were able to reflect on the geography of their neighborhoods and bring home go-kits, resources and activities to prepare with their pets, family members and neighbors.

### May 29, 2024 - Indian Tree Clubhouse

Neighborhood Leaders heard from a panel of their peers who shared strategies for organizing successful[block parties and gatherings](https://www.arvadaco.gov/483/Block-Party-Trailer-Outdoor-Movie-Equipm). Some of their tips included using a combination of in person and online marketing strategies for invitations/promotion and varying the dates/times of gatherings to allow for all ages to participate.
